newsitem.title: USA: Ohio governor pushes levy for Cleveland schools.
newsitem.headline: Ohio governor pushes levy for Cleveland schools.

text.p: Ohio Gov. George Voinovich formally announced his support Tuesday for a proposed 13.5 mill property tax levy on the Nov 5 ballot for Cleveland schools.
"Cleveland is at the crossroads, and this levy is an important step in helping to turn the Cleveland Public School system around," Voinovich said in a news release.
In August, a U.S. District Court judge in Cleveland ordered the proposed operating levy hike to be placed on the ballot after the Cleveland school board rejected a referendum to increase the levy.
The levy proposal was supported by Ohio Department of Education, which took control of the schools in March 1995.
State officials have said the levy was needed to improve services and to start paying off about $87 million of the school system's operating debt.
The 13.5 mill hike in the property tax levy would raise about $67.5 million a year.
Cleveland voters last passed an operating levy for the schools in November 1983.
